sources.title: Computer Vision for Clinical Gait Analysis: A Gait Abnormality Video Dataset
sources.version: Full text inspected: arXiv v1, 5 July 2024; 2025 publication metadata confirmed by author repository.
supports: The largest claim in section 3.2 concerns online-accessible abnormal-gait videos annotated by expert clinicians.

sources.title: The problem of pseudoreplication in neuroscientific studies: is it affecting your analysis?
supports: Distinct repeated observations can remain dependent.
Ignoring nesting can give false precision; an observational count need not equal the independent sample size.
does_not_establish: The magnitude of within-recording correlation in this study.

recommended_manuscript_wording: GAVD was introduced as the largest publicly accessible collection of abnormal-gait videos annotated by expert clinicians. It contains 1,874 normal and abnormal walking sequences. Our study evaluates 456 unique annotated walking sequences, using 2,815 forecast windows.
independence_wording: A gait sequence is a distinct observational unit. Sequences from the same recording or participant may remain dependent, so related sequences stay together in evaluation and uncertainty estimation.
largest_claim_status: Supported as an attributed claim with abnormal-gait RGB/video scope; not verified as a current cross-modality worldwide ranking.
limits: This was a targeted primary-source check, not an exhaustive 2026 census of all gait datasets.
Primary sources support the intended sequence definition; the local cohort audit must establish actual turn/view/overlap behavior.
Clinical visual annotations are meaningful expert labels, but they do not provide this study with patient records or independent diagnostic reassessment.
No acceptance probability or new p-value is estimated.
